Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: The jacket’s front panels are brought together so no visible opening remains along its closure.
node.binding: Compare the jacket on the woman in SOURCE with the jacket on the woman in EDITED; the requested endpoint is a fully closed jacket.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The jacket shows no requested progress toward closure compared with SOURCE.
node.half_when: The jacket is partly closed, with concrete progress toward closure but a visible opening remaining.
node.full_when: The jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its closure.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket is visibly open in SOURCE, with its front panels separated. In EDITED, it remains open and appears to flare apart as she turns; no closure is visible. There is no requested progress toward closing it.
